transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is... I’ve been arranging my whole day around avoiding certain drives, especially high bridges. Like, I’ll leave earlier, take a longer route, whatever I need to do so I don’t have to go over them. And if I can’t avoid it, I can still do it, but I’m gripping the wheel so tight my hands hurt, just trying to get across. It feels kind of ridiculous to say out loud, but it’s been affecting how I plan things.
Are there other situations or places, besides high bridges, that you actively avoid because of similar feelings of fear or anxiety?

Not really other places, no. It’s pretty much centered on those high bridges when I’m driving. I mean, I’ll plan my whole day around not having to go over one if I can help it — like checking routes, leaving earlier, taking some longer way that probably doesn’t make much sense to anybody else. And if I can’t avoid it, I do get across, but it’s not like I’m calm about it. I’m just white-knuckling the wheel the whole time, kind of holding my breath until I’m on the other side.

When you’re on one of those high bridges, do you ever feel like you’re having a panic attack, like your heart races, you feel dizzy, or like you can’t breathe, or is it more just a feeling of intense fear or discomfort without those physical symptoms?

It’s not like I totally lose control or anything, at least I don’t think so. But it comes on really fast. As soon as I see the bridge coming up, even before I’m actually on it, my chest kind of tightens up and my hands start sweating on the steering wheel. Then I get this feeling like I have to lock in and just stare straight ahead, like if I look anywhere else or think too much about it, I won’t make it across.

So… I don’t know if I’d call it a full panic attack, exactly. It’s more like this intense fear and discomfort that hits right away, and I’m just focused on getting to the other side.
When you're on or approaching a high bridge, are you more afraid of the height itself, or of something else like not being able to get off the bridge quickly if you start feeling anxious?

It’s more the height, I think… or maybe what the height makes me picture. I don’t really worry that I’ll be trapped there or that I can’t get off fast enough. It’s more like, even though I know those bridges over the bay are built fine, and people drive over them all day every day without anything happening, my mind just doesn’t treat it that way.

When I’m getting close to one, it’s like this thought pops in that the car could somehow go right over the side. I know that sounds dramatic, and logically I know there are barriers and the bridge isn’t just going to fall apart or anything, but that’s where my brain goes. I’ll be looking ahead and suddenly I’m very aware of how high up I am, how much space is around me, the water down there… and then I just want to keep the car perfectly straight and get across.
